meta.description: South-polar permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) from the LROC PSR Atlas and Lemelin 2021, and their host craters: cold-trap candidates with positions, sizes, temperatures and access data.
meta.coordinate_convention: Decimal degrees; latitude south negative; longitude east-positive, lon_east_180 (-180..180) and lon_east_360 (0..360). Where the notes gave only one form, the other was computed during conversion (+/-360).
meta.validation: Copied from research notes of 2026-11-14. Not validated by the science lead. A permanently shadowed region is a cold-trap candidate, not proof of ice.
source_meta_notes: Values copied from research notes of 2026-11-14; not independently validated.

Evidence classes (as in the notes): DIRECT = direct detection of H2O/volatiles; INDIRECT = hydrogen (neutrons), temperature/illumination models, albedo or radar proxies; MODEL = geological/thermal modelling; SPEC = speculation / press characterisation.

Item 'type' values: psr_atlas (LROC PSR Atlas, 40 largest south-polar PSRs), psr_lemelin2021 (per-PSR evidence and accessibility), lend_maximum (McClanahan 2024 Table 1), host_crater (centre/diameter), location_evidence (evidence matrix per location), dataset_finding (what each instrument found).
Lemelin's WEH column and McClanahan's LEND collimated WEH are DIFFERENT products; do not mix them in one numeric field without the instrument tag.
Lemelin 2021 temperature minima of 2 K (Shoemaker) and 14 K are 'as printed and look like data artefacts' per the notes.
Host-crater coordinates marked 'WP' come from Wikipedia infoboxes (which cite the IAU/USGS Gazetteer); Gazetteer-grade values were directly confirmed only for Cabeus and Amundsen.
Only one ground-truth direct detection of bulk water exists at the south pole (LCROSS, Cabeus). No landed mission has measured ice in situ at the south pole as of November 2026.
Surface-frost datasets (LAMP, LOLA, M3) are mutually inconsistent and do not correlate with the buried-hydrogen (neutron) dataset; ShadowCam 2026 finds no widespread surface ice above ~20-30 wt%.
